slides.title: Driftwood
slides.subtitle: Logistics infrastructure for direct-to-consumer furniture makers
slides.hook: Furniture makers want to sell direct. Freight makes them sell through someone else.
slides.notes: Seed round pitch, built for a quick send to angel investors. Keep delivery conversational - the deck should stand on its own if read without a call.

slides.title: Shipping a couch isn't like shipping a T-shirt
slides.hook: Freight, warehousing, and returns are built for big retailers - not a 10-person workshop.
bullets: Bulky, fragile items need freight carriers, white-glove delivery, and real warehousing
Small makers get worse freight rates and slower, less reliable delivery than large retailers
Handling logistics in-house pulls makers' time away from actually making furniture
Many makers cap their DTC ambitions or cobble together unreliable, costly workarounds

slides.title: We're the ops team furniture makers can't afford to hire
slides.hook: Makers plug into our network instead of negotiating with freight carriers themselves.
bullets: End-to-end logistics: warehousing, shipping, and returns, fully handled for the maker
Makers keep selling direct to consumers - we run everything after "order placed"
Simple pricing: a per-item fee plus a monthly storage fee
Makers stay focused on their craft instead of managing carriers and claims

slides.title: Early traction
slides.takeaway: At 42 makers growing 15% a month, the engine already works - this round adds the ops capacity to scale it without breaking it.

slides.title: We get paid on every shipment and every month of storage
slides.hook: Revenue scales with each maker's order volume and inventory footprint.
bullets: Per-item fee charged on every order we ship for a maker
Monthly storage fee for the inventory we warehouse
Blended average revenue per maker: $340/month across the current base
Revenue grows both as makers sell more and as the maker base grows

slides.title: Makers can build the product. They can't build a freight network.
slides.hook: Direct-to-consumer demand is here; the fulfillment infrastructure for small makers isn't.
bullets: DTC furniture sales keep growing, but freight, warehousing, and returns are still built for large retailers
Without affordable logistics, makers either turn away online orders or absorb costs that erode their margin
Driftwood lets a small maker operate like a direct-to-consumer brand without becoming a logistics company

slides.title: The next 12 months
slides.takeaway: Reaching 150 makers only requires an 11% monthly growth rate - slower than the 15% we're already sustaining.

slides.title: $1.2M to turn a 15%-a-month trend into a 150-maker platform
slides.hook: The constraint on growth isn't demand - it's hands-on ops capacity.
bullets: Raising a $1.2M seed round
Hire 2 operations specialists to run warehousing, shipping, and returns at scale
12 months of runway to grow from 42 to 150 makers on the platform
Funds the operational capacity growth requires, not just headcount for its own sake

slides.title: Let's build the logistics backbone furniture makers deserve
bullets: 42 makers today, growing 15% month over month for 4 straight months
$1.2M seed round to hire 2 ops specialists and reach 150 makers in 12 months
Let's talk this week
